Cal Hacks 13.0

This year's Cal Hacks is presented by Anthropic, Annapurna Labs, SpacetimeDB, and Hyphenate! Together we'll assemble in SF for a weekend of hacking, friendship, and crazy ideas.

[Join hackathon](https://cal-hacks-13-0.devpost.com/register?flow%5Bdata%5D%5Bchallenge_id%5D=29871\&flow%5Bname%5D=register_for_challenge)

Who can participate

Ages 18+ only

College students only

Team required: 2 to 4 members

All countries/territories, excluding standard exceptions

[View full rules](/rules)

October 25 at 12:00pm EDT to deadline

[View schedule](https://cal-hacks-13-0.devpost.com/details/dates)

Deadline: Oct 25, 2026 @ 9:00am PDT

Cal Hacks has always been about empowering students to build without boundaries!

We're so excited to have you join us for our 13th iteration of the world's largest collegiate hackathon! Here are some resources to help you this weekend:

Live Site: [Hive Platform](hive.hackberkeley.org)

Mobile Apps: [iOS App](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hackathons-berkeley/id6761351929) | [Android App](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.calhacks.hive\&pcampaignid=web_share)

Community Photo Album: [Google Photos](https://photos.app.goo.gl/BYdzzQJMn45bDYio6)

We really hope you enjoy the weekend! Feel free to come find us at the concierge desk near the entrence. Chat with any organizers walking around in white event shirts. Use the #ask-directors channel on Slack.

And, don't forget, go bears 🧸

Requirements

Get to the venue by October 25th @ 8 AM PST. You must've had been accepted and checked in as a hacker to submit.

You must submit your hack by October 25th @ 9 AM PST with your teammates! This is a hard deadline.

Include an image of your project and GitHub repository for any code to be considered.

All work must be done during the hackathon

You will have three minutes to pitch and two minutes for judges to ask questions.

You must have a pre-recorded or live demonstration.

\[MLH] Best Use of Tiger Data

1 winner

Stream Deck Mini || Building high-performance apps under hackathon deadlines shouldn't mean spending half your weekend configuring complex databases or learning obscure query languages. Tiger Data extends PostgreSQL to give student developers an ultra-fast foundation for real-time data, time-series metrics, and complex analytics.

Why build with Tiger Data this weekend?

Standard SQL Power: Query massive datasets instantly using the SQL you already know, with no complex NoSQL aggregation pipelines required.

Unified Data Stack: Store relational user profiles and high-frequency metric streams side-by-side in a single database.

Instant Dashboards: Serve lag-free, real-time frontend charts using pre-computed Continuous Aggregates.

90%+ Data Compression: Store millions of events on free-tier cloud instances without running out of disk space.

Whether you’re building real-time IoT monitoring, AI-driven analytics dashboards, or financial prediction engines, show us how Tiger Data powers your project. The team that demonstrates the most innovative, impactful, and performance-driven use of Tiger Data will take home some great prizes!

Judges

DDoSKi & his not-so judgy buddies

DDoSKi & his not-so judgy buddies
Cal Hacks 13.0

Judging Criteria

Application
Projects should have a feasible real-world use. Could someone realistically adopt this, and would it deliver a clear benefit? Strong submissions identify who they help, what problem they solve, and why people would actually use them.

Intentionality
Projects should offer an intuitive, engaging experience for their target users, guided by clear first principles. Every design choice should feel purposeful, with a clear sense of who it's for and why it works the way it does.

Functionality
Projects should work as intended, with a live demo that runs smoothly free of major bugs. Submissions should also include a clear, meaningful video demo on devpost for sponsors evaluating asynchronously.

Creativity
Projects should show original thinking and a fresh perspective, with inventive problem framing and unexpected combinations of ideas or technologies. Clearly show what makes your project stand out from similar work.

Technical Complexity
Teams should show a command of the frameworks and infrastructure behind their project, with sound architectural choices and engineering depth that goes beyond basic implementation.
